correctness.rationale: For fixed half-sides, the coefficient law is independent of c: constant Jacobian in area, and ordered side weights a/(2(a+b)), b/(2(a+b)) on the boundary. Separate coordinate reflection makes J=2ab ΔW ΔV symmetric conditional on the diagonal contribution D and |J|. With θ=(1+c1/c2)/2, each D±c1|J| is a convex combination of D±c2|J| with exchanged weights. Strict Jensen applies on |J|>0, which occurs almost surely in area and with positive probability on opposite parallel edges in the boundary model. Direct second moments give the two c-independent means. Subtracting mz²/2 from the test function gives the deficit (m/2)(c2²−c1²)E[J²] by convex order; the two E[J²] values follow from E[(ΔW)²(ΔV)²]=4/9 in area, and 2E[W²V²]+2E[W²]E[V²]=4/3+8ab/(9(a+b)²) on the boundary. Quadratic tests attain equality. I separately checked these slopes by tensor three-node Gauss–Legendre integration over the side-pair and area-pair coordinates (polynomials of degree at most four per coordinate); at (a,b)=(2,1) the slopes of E[Z²] versus c² were 7.1111111111 and 24.4938271605, respectively. On collapse, each of the two boundary routes from −(a+b) to a+b projects monotonically, with common arclength density; the resulting uniform law yields the stated triangular difference density and moment formula. Nonattainment of extremal needle values pertains to p≠2; p=2 is explicitly constant in the Finding. The supplied script was inspected, not run.
residual_risks: The needle law uses the limit of boundary arclength sampling with fixed positive sides; do not apply it to area sampling or infer ordinary stochastic dominance.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the fixed-side angular convex ordering of the squared two-point distance, in both sampling models, including strictness and its quantitative deficit. Prior fourth-moment formulae are not novel, and the exact quadratic deficit uses that moment information together with the new order. The sharp boundary mean/perimeter lower bound 1/6 and a needle limit realizing sharpness are already known; credit here only the fixed-side shear mechanism and full limiting law and power moments, not the bare 1/6 bound.

value.rationale: A comparison of full laws answers a more informative geometric question than one or two moments: the equal-mean squared chord becomes more dispersed for every fixed-side shear, both in area and on the boundary. It explains the complete reversal at p=2 with strict extrema and sharp quantitative control. The distinction from varying aspect ratio or switching sampling measures matters for using the result in shape comparisons.
residual_risks: The value assessment does not credit the already-known sharp global p=1 perimeter constant as new.
